category_title: Students who seek autonomy and independent mastery
student_description: Amir is a highly independent learner who thrives on autonomy and explicit real-world relevance but quickly abandons tasks if he feels micromanaged. The evidence reveals he uniquely needs instructors to provide upfront boundaries and materials, get him started, and then step back entirely, offering help only when explicitly requested rather than guiding him step-by-step.

criteria.rationale: Amir rejects generic justifications for learning (e.g., 'you will need this someday') and requires explicit connections to his actual life to value the material.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan must explicitly connect the subject matter to specific, concrete real-world uses or personal interests rather than relying on general academic requirements.

criteria.rationale: Amir needs to see the big picture from the beginning so he can self-assess and self-guide his learning journey.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term strategy must include providing a comprehensive roadmap, syllabus, or set of materials upfront (e.g., a course binder) rather than drip-feeding assignments day by day.
